name: orb_atr_scaled_5s
author: adapted from claude-4.6-opus-fast
thesis: Standard ORB uses fixed multiples of the opening range for targets and stops (e.g., 2x range). This ignores the stock's current volatility regime — on high-vol days the target should be wider, on low-vol days tighter. By scaling ORB targets and stops using ATR(14) on 1-min bars instead of the ORB range itself, we adapt the trade management to the stock's real-time volatility. The ORB level provides the entry signal, but ATR provides the trade management framework. Target = 2.0 * ATR_14, stop = 1.0 * ATR_14 regardless of ORB width. This decouples entry (ORB, which is about price structure) from management (ATR, which is about volatility reality). The inefficiency exists because most ORB implementations tightly couple entry levels with exit levels, creating inconsistent risk-reward across volatility regimes.
mechanism: The opening range concentrates pending orders and stop-losses on both sides. When price breaches the range boundary, stop-loss orders from wrong-side participants cascade, amplifying the move. Breakout-following algorithms detect the breach and add momentum, creating a self-reinforcing move that typically persists for 60-180 seconds before the order book absorbs the flow.

exit.signal_exit: if ADX_14 drops below 15 during trade (trend fading), exit

filters.vix_filter: India_VIX between 12 and 25 (wide range because ATR-scaling adapts to vol)
filters.expiry_filter: skip F&O expiry; skip earnings day

weaknesses: ATR_14 on 1-min bars is noisy in the first 15-30 minutes of the session; the ATR target/stop calculated at ORB breakout time may not reflect the stock's true volatility for the rest of the session
The fixed 2:1 RR ratio via ATR doesn't account for market structure; sometimes the next support/resistance is at 1.5x ATR, making the 2x target unrealistic
On low-vol days where ATR_14 is very small (< 0.1% of price), the ATR target can be only 10-15 bps, and after costs the trade is unprofitable even when it hits target
prior_art: Wilder (1978) ATR; Kaufman (2013) on ATR-based trade management. Van Tharp (1998) on ATR-based position sizing. Applied to ORB framework from Crabel (1990).
adaptation_notes: Converted from 1min to 5s bars. Lookback multiplier: 12x. Adaptations: timeframe scaling to 5-second candles; signal conversion from individual stock to NIFTY/BANKNIFTY index; lookback period scaling for 5-second bars; stop/target recalibration for 5-second timeframe. Stop/target calibrated for options point-based exits. Universe narrowed to NIFTY index.
